metric.definition: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.

reading.body:
Server utilization rate measures the share of provisioned compute doing real work over time, not at peak. It is the denominator that makes every efficiency metric honest.

Idle servers still consume power, licenses, and depreciation while producing nothing. That makes utilization a financial metric as much as a technical one. In most enterprise estates the money hides in the gap between what is provisioned and what is actually used.

For AI specifically, the metric matters because compute is the input that everything else depends on. A fleet running well below its provisioned capacity is paying for buildings and power that produce no output. Raising utilization is one of the few ways to expand effective compute without adding new capacity.

The data here defines the metric and places it in the Capacity and server use category alongside stranded power and space per cabinet, and floor loading limits. It does not give a target utilization rate, a current industry figure, or a method for measuring over time rather than at peak. Those are the numbers a reader would need to judge any particular fleet.
